<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918964_theRebbe_845" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918964_theRebbe_845__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The main judgment occurs when the limited kindness allotted on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur is insufficient for all needs, requiring a tzaddik's prayer to redirect it.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the main judgment and verdict regarding which matter the kindness will be drawn is when the kindness that was allotted to him on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur is extremely limited,</t>
    <t s="2">so that it is insufficient to draw from it all three matters of children, life, and sustenance, but only two of them or one of them,</t>
    <t s="3">for then there is judgment and verdict whether the flow of kindness will be in children, or in life, or in sustenance.</t>
    <t s="4">And the prayer of the tzaddik is effective to change it from one matter to another.</t>
    <t s="5">[As in the story about the Baal Shem Tov,</t>
    <t s="6">that childless people came to him to ask him to pray to G-d that they should have children,</t>
    <t s="7">and that man was a great wealthy man,</t>
    <t s="8">and the Baal Shem Tov said that if they agree to become poor, they will have children.</t>
    <t s="9">And when they accepted this upon themselves,</t>
    <t s="10">children were born to them and they became poor.</t>
    <t s="11">That is, the Baal Shem Tov saw that the kindness allotted to them would not suffice for both children and wealth together,</t>
    <t s="12">and through his prayer he effected a change of the flow of kindness from wealth to children.]</t>
    <t s="13">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="14">that then,</t>
    <t s="15">[when the kindness is limited so that it does not suffice for all the matters of children, life, and sustenance],</t>
    <t s="16">the judgment and verdict is most intense.</t>
    <t s="17">And in order for the kindness to be changed from one matter to another, it is specifically through the prayer of a tzaddik.</t>
    <t s="18">But in general, even when the kindness suffices for all three matters of children, life, and sustenance,</t>
    <t s="19">there is judgment and verdict every day regarding every particular flow,</t>
    <t s="20">and therefore we pray every day the twelve intermediate blessings, which contain requests for all things.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Although judgment on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur concerns the person as he is below in this world, he is also judged daily regarding how the allotted kindness will be drawn and whether it will be drawn in this world or above.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And it must be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">the judgment on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur is concerning the person as he is below</t>
    <t s="3">(soul in body)</t>
    <t s="4">[and particularly according to what is brought in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="5">from the Hagahos Maimoni,</t>
    <t s="6">that a person is judged on Rosh Hashanah regarding matters of this world],</t>
    <t s="7">and the judgment and verdict is</t>
    <t s="8">(not only regarding the flow of kindness in general,</t>
    <t s="9">but also)</t>
    <t s="10">regarding the particulars,</t>
    <t s="11">[and as is also evident from the fact that in the prayers of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur we also ask for particular matters],</t>
    <t s="12">and nevertheless, a person is judged every day regarding which matter the kindness that was allotted to him on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur will be drawn to him,</t>
    <t s="13">and furthermore,</t>
    <t s="14">he is judged whether the flow that was allotted to him will be drawn in this world or whether they will add for him delight etc. above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This is understood through the explanation in the Siddur on the verse "day to day utters speech," that on weekdays there are delays in drawing down the flow, like a person whose intellectual decision does not compel action and requires renewed deliberation for actual deed.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood according to what is explained in the Siddur</t>
    <t s="2">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="3">"Day to day utters speech,"</t>
    <t s="4">that on weekdays there are several delays in the drawing down of the flow below,</t>
    <t s="5">and on the day of Shabbos,</t>
    <t s="6">the drawing down of the flow is with speed,</t>
    <t s="7">"yavia omer,"</t>
    <t s="8">"yavia" connotes speed.</t>
    <t s="9">And it is explained there,</t>
    <t s="10">that this matter, that on weekdays it is possible that the flow will be delayed and not be drawn below,</t>
    <t s="11">is like a parable of a person who deliberates in his intellect about some matter, whether it is proper to do it or not, and comes to a conclusion and decision that it is proper to do it,</t>
    <t s="12">and nevertheless, it is possible that this will remain in his intellect and not come into actual deed.</t>
    <t s="13">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="14">that when the matter comes to actual deed, he weighs in his mind once again whether to actually do as he decided in his intellect.</t>
    <t s="15">For although the decision in the intellect was that it is proper to do the thing,</t>
    <t s="16">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="17">since the action that is felt by him in his intellectual decision is an action as it is included in the intellect,</t>
    <t s="18">therefore,</t>
    <t s="19">when the matter comes to actual deed,</t>
    <t s="20">an action as it is in itself</t>
    <t s="21">(separate from the intellect),</t>
    <t s="22">he must consult and deliberate in his intellect once again whether to actually do so.</t>
    <t s="23">And in particular,</t>
    <t s="24">there are two matters in this.</t>
    <t s="25">That the decision of the intellect</t>
    <t s="26">(that it is proper to do the thing)</t>
    <t s="27">does not compel the action,</t>
    <t s="28">for since the action included in the intellect and the actual deed</t>
    <t s="29">(as it is in itself, separate from the intellect)</t>
    <t s="30">are two matters,</t>
    <t s="31">therefore it is possible that the intellectual decision will not bring him to action,</t>
    <t s="32">meaning that he will not even think regarding the actual deed.</t>
    <t s="33">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="34">that even when he does think about it,</t>
    <t s="35">it is possible that he will have a reasoning not to do it,</t>
    <t s="36">and he must deliberate once again.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
